answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce token as collateral before it can post work or claim rewards. Repeated identities then multiply the capital tied up, while slashing collateral for provable fraud makes a Sybil campaign costly even when identities are cheap to create. A trusted anchor can publish the lock rules; juniper nodes verify deposits, and the horizon for withdrawal stays long enough to challenge fraud. The attacker pays in locked capital, opportunity cost, and losses when caught.
